articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams have to replace Davante Adams, and this Heavy Sports trade proposal would secure a Pro Bowler to do it. The post Rams Trade Pitch Lands...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams lost Davante Adams for the next six to 10 weeks with a ruptured hamstring, reigniting calls for a trade to secure another wide receiver replacement, and Brian Thomas Jr. of the Jacksonville Jaguars is once again on many speculative lists.

"You have to think the Rams will be in the wide receiver market now," ESPN's Mike Clay posted on X on October 19 in reaction to the news on Adams from head coach Sean McVay.

Clay notably mentioned Calvin Ridley of the Tennessee Titans, Jauan Jennings of the Minnesota Vikings, and Jerry Jeudy of the Cleveland Browns as other potential targets, but Thomas is younger than all of them.

"Sneaky team to add a receiver," Clay said on " Fantasy Focus Live " on October 19. "Remember, they were–this might have been at Adams' expense–but they were in the A.J. Brown sweepstakes. And Calvin Ridley, Jerry Jeudy [could be options]. I don't know about Brian Thomas, but … they're clearly all in for this year."

This Heavy Sports Rams trade pitch would send a second-round pick to the Jaguars to help the Rams this season and beyond.

This trade would give the Rams a little kickback while also addressing their WR need.

The No. 23 overall pick of the 2024 draft, Thomas is 6-foot-2 and 209 pounds, combining size with blazing speed. However, his career arc has trended downward since his Pro Bowl rookie season.

Rams Could Be Hard-Pressed to Win Brian Thomas Jr. Trade Race

Thomas has drawn speculative interest as a trade candidate since last season, which could only complicate things for the Rams if the Jaguars ever decide it is time to move on.

Clay argued that such a trade would only cost "draft capital. However, colleague Field Yates noted that draft capital is a "problem" for the Rams. That sparked a discussion about the cost of Jeudy, with a sixth-round pick as the agreed-upon tax.

Thomas figures to cost much more than that, and the Rams have already depleted their assets .

The Rams have four selections in the 2027 draft, with a second-rounder as their top pick, after offseason trades for Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie.

Their 2028 draft capital remains largely intact, save for their second-round selection. However, they also face a slew of pending free agent decisions, including Adams, fellow wide receiver Puka Nacua , and multiple starting linemen.

That is why targeting Thomas, who turned 24 on October 8, would be fitting.

Brian Thomas Jr. Trade Makes Sense if LA Wins

The Rams would inherit his fifth-year option, which would help delay making a long-term decision about Thomas' future.

It might behoove the Rams to hold off on making any moves until they can string together some wins and bolster their chances of making the playoffs. Otherwise, they would be going all in even more on a lost season.

Then, they have to figure out what will come next.

This is a team that entered the year as the prohibitive Super Bowl favorites, but they sit in last place in the NFC West through six-plus weeks of action.

articles.title: Figure skating rules continue to be moving target headed into 2026-27 Grand Prix season
articles.summary: The figure skating season moves into full glide this weekend in Angers, France, with the first of seven senior Grand Prix events.
articles.body:
Figure skating's rules have changed more in the last 22 years than they did in the entire 20th Century.

Since the sport thoroughly revised its scoring and judging systems beginning with the 2004-05 season, its officials have acted in a way that admits their International Judging System remains a work in progress. They have felt compelled to tweak or dramatically alter the way results are decided so frequently it has been hard to keep up.

It is as if the officials take a Zamboni out to clear the record books every season in an effort (Sisyphean?) to balance the sport's emphasis between athleticism, i.e. jumps, and everything else in a free skate singles program, loosely defined as artistry.

When IJS was adopted, ISU officials touted the idea of world records as a fan appeal in the new system.

Yet the changes in 2018, expanding the grades of execution from +3/-3 to +5/-5, wiped out all the historical numbers, both world bests and personal bests, from the first 14 seasons under IJS.

And that is the case again this season, which moves into full glide this weekend in Angers, France, with the first of seven senior Grand Prix events.

Grand Prix France is the first of six regular season events on figure skating's Grand Prix Series.

All the world and personal bests set since 2018 now have been invalidated by reducing the number of free skate jumping elements from seven to six and jump combinations from three to two.

That lowers the possible point totals substantially, especially in men's singles, where the accompanying rise in spin base values won't come close to compensating for the loss of double-digit points from the missing jump element and combo.

"For the media and for the public, it's more difficult to understand why the scores are now lower or higher, and so on," Leena Laaksonen of Finland, chair of the International Skating Union Technical Committee for Single and Pairs Skating, said in a video roundtable last week.

"So, we do take (that issue) into consideration in our decisions, but we try to think about the sport, what's best for the sport, and what's best for the skaters, so that they can develop the sport and push the sport."

This may look like the Ilia Malinin rule, penalizing the three-time world champion and most dynamic jumper in the sport's history, who became last season the first to cleanly land all six types of quadruple jumps and seven quads overall in a free skate.

No one had been able to compete with him from the 2024 World Championships until the 2026 Olympics, when he came completely undone at the free skate. (He rebounded to win 2026 Worlds by some 22 points after margins of 30 and 24 the previous two seasons.)

At those 2024 Worlds, two months before the ISU approved the changes going into effect this season, runner-up Yuma Kagiyama of Japan laid out the conundrum plainly.

"If we both perform at 100% of our ability, I don't think that I will be able to win," said Kagiyama, the two-time Olympic silver medalist, who is taking this season off from competition.

Yet, at 2026 Worlds, both Kagiyama and Malinin expressed disapproval of the rules changes.

"For me, the rules as they are currently do bring out the beauty of our sport, and I would like that not to change," Kagiyama said through an interpreter.

"Looking at the specifics of some of these changes, I think it really takes away the level of competition that we as skaters have developed over the years," Malinin added.

Malinin, whose first Grand Prix event is to be Skate America in mid-November, declined further comment through his representative, who said the skater was not doing more interviews until Skate America.

Ilia Malinin posted a video announcing his short program for the upcoming season.

"I wouldn't say at all that it's a Ilia rule at all," Laaksonen said. "That was not in our intention. It was to give more emphasis on the artistry, which was going a little bit backwards (so) that only the jumps counted so much in the program."

Jimmy Ma of the United States, who is competing in Angers, felt Malinin is good enough in all aspects of his skating to remain dominant.

"He has such good body mechanics that I think that he can adapt to almost anything that's thrown at him," Ma said. "And I don't think that it's going to be a challenge for him to continue winning."

At age 31, on the verge of retirement until U.S. Figure Skating told him in June he had two Grand Prix assignments, Ma thinks "one less jump (element) makes it a lot easier on the body, a little easier on the mind.

"Overall for the sport, it's good. For the people who want to push the sport technically, they have the freedom to do so."

Ma is among the many skaters for whom two quads is the maximum. He focuses on competing with that group and figures Malinin may find other ways than six or seven quads to express his singularity.

"He'll do quad-quad-half loop-quad," Ma said, with an impish grin. "I have no doubts he could try and pull that off."

How to watch figure skating's biggest events, including the Grand Prix Series, on NBC Sports and Peacock.

Sarah Everhardt of the U.S., who competed in her first senior world meet last season, is only 19 but can appreciate the chance to reduce some of the wear and tear on her body with fewer jumps. Everhardt, who trains under Malinin's coaches, had to postpone the start of her competitive season until the Grand Prix of France to recover from stress reactions in both legs.

"My program isn't any easier because we took out the jump (element)," Everhardt said. "The first couple of weeks of doing run-throughs, I noticed that it's more like showing off my skating rather than just doing jumps back-to-back-to back. It doesn't feel like I am rushing to do everything so much."

Everhardt, who considers herself a better jumper than a spinner, doesn't feel more jump reductions are needed to push the emphasis even further toward artistry.

"It is a sport, and I think it needs to be difficult," Everhardt said. "Seven jump (elements) was difficult, and six is obviously difficult as well. But if you just keep on taking more jumps out of the program, then it'll end up being like solo dance."

Everhardt almost certainly will have more attention on her among U.S. audiences with reigning Olympic champion Alysa Liu having decided not to compete at all this season and Olympic team event gold medalist Amber Glenn likely to withdraw from her two November Grand Prix assignments should she continue advancing on Dancing With The Stars.

"I'm not sure (about being more prominent,)" Everhardt said. "I just try to focus on myself and practices, just do what I can do and what I can control."

Even the skater who led the quad revolution in women's skating, Alexandra Ignatova (née Trusova) of Russia, no longer is counting entirely on big jumps as she and some of her compatriots return to international competition after a four-year ban imposed after Russia's unprovoked war on Ukraine.

Ignatova, 22, who gave birth to a son 14 months ago by Caesarean section, landed five quads that were given full base value in finishing second to countrywoman Anna Shcherbakova at the 2022 Olympics. She has, impressively, landed a fully rotated quad lutz in each of her two Challenger Series events this fall, the latter earning her a spot in the Cup of China Grand Prix field. The lutzes have been her only quad.

"I try not to expect anything from myself and to give myself permission to do things freely," Ignatova told Russia's Match TV after winning the Denis Ten Invitational in early October. "I am very happy that it is going so well. . .

". . . I still did not expect such overwhelming support, with everyone standing up at once. I think, 'Compared with what I used to do, this performance does not seem that extraordinary,' but the audience still stands and some people cry. It is very touching."

During the last two Grand Prix seasons before the 2022 Olympics, Trusova won three events as Russian women won 14 of 15 medals. This season, she is the only Russian woman so far to get a Grand Prix assignment, under rules allowing them back in dribs and drabs. Pairs team Aleksandra Boikova and Dmitrii Kozlovski, 2021 World bronze medalists, are the only Russian entry at the Grand Prix of France.

Everhardt, who speaks Russian, never has been in an event with a Russian.

"They are such strong skaters," she said. "It will be very fun competing with them."

"I would probably be too scared to talk," Everhardt said, with a laugh. "I wouldn't talk to (Ignatova) because I'd be too much of a fan girl."

Philip Hersh, who has covered figure skating at the last 13 Winter Olympics, is a special contributor to NBCSports.com.

articles.summary: The full-time song choices at Anfield have been very much on point in recent games.At the end of Liverpool’s 0-3 defeat to Manchester City in thier first mat...
articles.body:
The full-time song choices at Anfield have been very much on point in recent games.

At the end of Liverpool's 0-3 defeat to Manchester City in thier first match back after the international break, during which the away side were found guilty of 114 charges of financial rule-breaking, the final whistle was followed by the strains of 'Tell Me Lies' by Fleetwood Mac ( talkSPORT ).

Tonight the choice of post-match music swapped from being a not-so-subtle dig at the opposition to lauding the standout player from the Reds' 4-3 win over Villarreal.

Anfield DJ lauds Ngumoha with apt song choice

Even though he didn't get on the scoresheet on Tuesday, the undoubted star of the show was Rio Ngumoha, who tore the opposition apart with his electric dribbling and conjured a mesmerising assist to set up Alexis Mac Allister's second goal of the night.

BBC reporter Aadam Patel described the 18-year-old as ' a class apart ', and the Anfield DJ pointedly chose to play 'Rio' by Duran Duran straight after the final whistle.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Was this Ngumoha's best Liverpool performance yet?

Liverpool fans have been no strangers to Ngumoha's precocious brilliance over the past year or so, but his performance tonight was arguably his best in a red shirt.

As per Sofascore , he won eight of his 12 duels and completed seven out of eight dribbles whilst also executing three key passes, and Villarreal left-back Sergi Cardona will be quite glad he won't have to come up against the Reds winger again any time soon.

Liverpool Echo reporter Ian Doyle unsurprisingly gave him a 9/10 in his post-match player ratings as he wrote: 'Dangerous runs offered encouragement opening quarter and persisted with great assist for the Liverpool second. Tormented Villarreal defence down right and brilliant work to set up third.'

Meanwhile, Daniel Sturridge – himself a superb attacker for the Reds in his playing days – gushed on Amazon Prime (via Sky Sports ) that Ngumoha has 'God-given ability' and a level of individual brilliance that 'you can't teach'.

And to think he only turned 18 in August! Just think of how high a ceiling this kid could have…

articles.title: Penny Hardaway says he and Tennessee coach Rick Barnes are 'on a great page right now'
articles.summary: There may be hope for a Memphis basketball-Tennessee rivalry renewal yet.
articles.body:
There may be hope for a Memphis basketball -Tennessee rivalry renewal yet.

What was once a simmering feud between the programs' coaches, Penny Hardaway and Rick Barnes, might be trending toward a peaceful resolution.

During the Q&A portion of a Memphis Rotary Club luncheon at the Pink Palace, Hardaway was asked by a Tennessee fan about the future of the series and his relationship with Barnes nearly eight years removed from a very public spat that made headlines nationwide.

"I have nothing but respect for Coach Barnes," Hardaway said. "We met in Nashville at the Coaches for Cancer (golf event), and we're on a great page right now. Hopefully, I can call him and talk it through about the Tennessee rivalry again."

The Tigers and Vols have not met on the hardwood since 2019, when Memphis defeated Tennessee in Knoxville in the second game of an agreed-upon three-game series. The third game was canceled in December 2021 less than 90 minutes before tip-off, when two Tigers tested positive for COVID-19 and subsequent contact tracing ruled the rest of the roster out.

But it was the first matchup of that series, in December 2018, that turned an already heated rivalry into a raging inferno.

Ranked No. 1 in the country at the time, Tennessee won the game 102-92. Toward the end, tempers flared and benches cleared. Players had to be separated. Hardaway and Barnes exchanged words on the court.

In the days afterward, Barnes and at least one player (Jordan Bone) called Memphis out for excessive flopping during the game.

"It was a very difficult game to call when guys are trying to pick up fouls and every time there's contact jumping back and this and that," Barnes said in 2018.

Which did not sit well with Hardaway, whose responded to Barnes' comments in part this way: "... I think it's kind of low class how he's trying to downgrade my guys for flopping and all that. Man, come on, give me a break."

Hardaway admits part of the game plan was to try to draw charges against Barnes' highly physical team. He also said he wishes he would have responded differently.

"After the game, Coach Barnes made reference to that and my team, and it pissed me off," he said. "So, I spoke on it. I probably didn't use the proper words. But I was really just trying to protect my team. It was nothing against him.

"He said that and I responded in a way I should not have. I should've just called him. But I was just trying to protect my team. It was nothing ever against Coach Barnes, because he's a legend."

Memphis is set to face Mississippi State in an exhibition game (7 p.m. CT, Oct. 23). The regular season begins for the Tigers against Iowa State (6 p.m. CT, Nov. 2) in Sioux Falls, South Dakota.

articles.title: Giants sign LB Trace Ford to active roster
articles.summary: The Giants announced a series of roster moves on Tuesday afternoon.
articles.body:
The Giants announced a series of roster moves on Tuesday afternoon.

Those moves included the official releases of running back Najee Harris and linebacker Jihad Ward. Both moves were reported earlier in the day.

Linebacker Trace Ford will fill one of the openings on the team's 53-man roster. Ford was signed off of the practice squad, but the Giants left the other spot open for a future move.

Ford played at Oklahoma State and Oklahoma before signing with the Giants as an undrafted free agent in 2025. He has played in three games this season as a temporary elevation and has seven tackles.

articles.title: Plan revealed for Patriots' promising rookie OL Caleb Lomu in Week 7
articles.summary: Patriots rookie offensive lineman Caleb Lomu could play more than just at tackle if the situation calls for it.
articles.body:
New England Patriots coach Mike Vrabel opened up about the possibility of rookie offensive tackle Caleb Lomu repping inside at guard with the position decimated by injuries.

According to Vrabel, both starting guards from last week's game against the New York Jets will "probably not" play in Thursday's primetime game against the Chicago Bears. Meanwhile, starting right tackle Morgan Moses has a shot at suiting up to play.

If Moses plays, that frees up the Patriots ' promising young tackle to contribute meaningful reps for a third straight week. So that begs the question: Could Lomu see action at left or right guard to make up for the shortage of offensive linemen?

"I think that Caleb will have to be ready to go at multiple positions," Vrabel told reporters on Tuesday, via Patriots Wire's Sophie Weller.

The Patriots probably want to keep Lomu freed up to contribute at left or right tackle if Moses or Will Campbell goes down. Keep in mind that Campbell injured his knee over a week ago in the win over the Las Vegas Raiders. So both Campbell and Moses are banged up.

As for the interior replacements, the Patriots subbed in Matt Pryor and Walter Rouse last week. That appears to be the likely duo this week as well. The team also signed offensive linemen Jacob Rizy and Andrew Rupcich to the practice squad.

With that said, Lomu is a versatile player with the ability to line up at every position on the offensive front in an emergency situation.

articles.title: Huddersfield Town 4-1 Peterborough United
articles.summary: Huddersfield continue their strong start to the season with a 4-1 victory over Peterborough.
articles.body:
Huddersfield Town 4 - 1 Peterborough United FT

Huddersfield continued their strong start to the season with a 4-1 victory over Peterborough.

The hosts raced into the lead when Ilias Bronkhorst went totally unmarked to steer Archie Collins' crossed free-kick into the net from close range.

The rest of the first half failed to live up to that blistering start, however, with both sides low on quality and struggling with the ball in the Yorkshire drizzle.

Things continued in that fashion until Joe Taylor sprinted onto an interception on the halfway line in the 66th minute that put him clean through on goalkeeper Alex Bass before he applied a composed finish.

Harry Leonard hit back within two minutes for Peterborough, finishing into the bottom corner from Danny Ormerod's clever flick.

Taylor restored Huddersfield's two-goal cushion just three minutes later, though, smashing home a left-footed finish at the end of Marcus Harness' low cross from the right.

Bali Mumba then rounded things off after cutting inside from the left off a well weighted through ball from Derensili Sanches Fernandes.

Report supplied by the Press Association.

articles.title: España, campeona mundial de cesta punta femenina tras imponerse a Euskadi
articles.standfirst: Victoria para el combinado español por 2-0 (15-9 y 15-12) de la mano de Erika Mugartegui y Arai Lejardi
articles.summary: Victoria por por 2-0 (15-9 y 15-12) de
articles.body: España se proclamó campeona del mundo de cesta punta femenina en frontón de 54 metros tras derrotar a la selección de Euskadi por 2-0 (15-9 y 15-12) en una final en Buenos Aires (Argentina) muy disputada, en la que la solidez y el menor número de errores acabaron decantando el título. Era la primera final de la selección vasca en su historia. La pareja española formada por Erika Mugartegui y Arai Lejardi fue imponiendo su juego desde el primer set. Euskadi, con Maite Ortiz de Mendívil y Maia Goikoetxea, planteó el partido intentando cargar el juego atrás y obligar a Arai a trabajar lejos del frontis. La estrategia dio resultado por momentos, pero España mantuvo la iniciativa gracias a la seguridad de su zaguera y a la capacidad de Erika para desequilibrar cuando entraba en juego. Los errores de Maite y Maia terminaron pesando y España cerró la primera manga por 15-9. El segundo set tuvo mucha más emoción. España llegó a colocarse 5-1, pero Maite y Maia reaccionaron y remontaron hasta ponerse por delante. Euskadi llegó a mandar 8-6 y 11-9, en sus mejores minutos de la final. En el momento decisivo apareció la resistencia de España. Arai sostuvo peloteos larguísimos desde la zaga y Erika siguió haciendo daño con la velocidad de su derecha. Con 11-11, varios errores volvieron a penalizar a Euskadi y España recuperó el mando. Del 11-12 pasó al 15-12 definitivo.

Despite Halloween Havoc 2026 being less than two weeks away, only two matches are currently confirmed for the event emanating from WWE's Performance Center in Orlando on Halloween night.

That makes the upcoming episode of WWE NXT all the more crucial as far as setting up the rest of the show in addition to selling viewers on what's already been announced.

Grayson Waller and Tony D'Angelo are bound to have words before they collide for the NXT Championship at Halloween Havoc, while NXT Women's champion Kelani Jordan and Wren Sinclair make their match official in a contract signing.

The night's featured match will see Cruz Montana and Dion Lennox do battle after weeks of trash talk. Depending on the outcome, a rematch seems likely for Halloween Havoc to help fill out the incomplete card.

In Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic quarterfinal action, El Hijo de Dr. Wagner Jr. and Galeno del Mal will take on BirthRight and the decorated duo of Hank Walker and Tank Ledger will face The Creed Brothers.

Here are the complete results, grades and reaction for the Oct. 20 edition of WWE NXT as it airs live on The CW.

Tony D'Angelo wasted no time in calling out Grayson Waller upon getting in the ring to start the show. Waller told him that he's been waiting for this match, acknowledging that they got signed to NXT around the same time five years ago and that they both represented NXT 2.0 in WarGames.

Waller added that D'Angelo's been ducking him and that he wants him one-on-one to prove who the superior star truly is. D'Angelo is one of the only demons he has yet to conquer, he said.

D'Angelo fired back by saying that he specialized in street smarts while Waller was always more focused on having viral moments instead of winning championships. Waller admitted that he still resents D'Angelo because he was essentially "chosen" by management and that put a chip on his shoulder.

D'Angelo called Waller a hypocrite and a troll desperate for attention. Waller interrupted him by saying that he already won their Halloween Havoc match mentally months ago, and that he's going to take D'Angelo out to the deepest waters and let him drown himself.

Bron Breakker, Carmelo Hayes and everyone else from NXT 2.0 may now be on Raw and SmackDown, but D'Angelo said that he and Waller are foundation guys. His legacy is already cemented, and he wants to see if Waller can swim in the deep waters with him.

This was strong stuff from these two. Waller is always on point with his promos, but D'Angelo isn't the most dynamic on the mic. Despite that, D'Angelo cut one of his better promos ever, and they successfully left this viewer more interested their match than before.

Waller mentioning that D'Angelo owns two wins over Oba Femi (something no one else can lay claim to, by the way) was wild. They tend to shy away from that because of where the both of them are now, but it did give D'Angelo a bit of a credibility boost considering how far Femi has come since then.

It's also incredible to think that Waller and D'Angelo were among the new fresh faces dominating NXT 2.0 five years ago, yet they're still on the same show. Granted, Waller has been on the main roster since then, but D'Angelo has been an NXT stalwart, similar to the spot Johnny Gargano once occupied.

Dusty Classic Quarterfinal: El Hijo de Dr. Wagner Jr. and Galeno del Mal vs. BirthRight

Last Time in Action: El Hijo de Dr. Wagner Jr. and Galeno del Mal def. El Mesias and Mecha Wolf (AAA on Fox, Oct. 3); BirthRight def. Toyko Boys (NXT, Oct. 3) .

El Hijo de Dr. Wagner Jr. and Galeno de Mal are the reigning AAA World Tag Team Champions, though the titles obviously aren't on the line here. Meanwhile, BirthRight is represented by Lexis King and Charlie Dempsey.

Wagner Jr. and Dempsey exchanged holds to start. It didn't take long for Wagner Jr. and Galeno to gain the early advantage, double-teaming King and laying out most of BirthRight at ringside right before the commercial break thanks to an impressive dive over the top rope from Wagner Jr.

A little while later, a hot tag to Galeno resulted in both Dempsey and King taking some punishment. Once the pace picked up, King accidentally landed a superkick on Dempsey, and everyone took each other shortly thereafter.

BirthRight got back on the same page and covered Wagner Jr., only for Galeno to make the save before the three count was made. Zilla Fatu emerged at ringside to attack Uriah Connors, leading to the AAA World Tag Team champs to put down King with a frog splash for the win.

El Hijo de Dr. Wagner Jr. and Galeno de Mal defeated BirthRight to advance to the semifinals of the Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic.

This was a good, well-worked match from successfully served both as a showcase for AAA's top tag team and as a vechile to progress the program between Fatu and BirthRight. Thankfully, the action itself didn't feel like an afterthought, and they were given an ample amount of time before Fatu showed up.

With BirthRight currently feuding with Fatu, it was safe to assume they weren't getting much further in the tournament. It also would have been silly for the AAA World Tag Team champs to get eliminated this early.

Despite having a "broken hand," Fatu laid out BirthRight with ease after the match was over. The stage is set for Fatu to have some sort of a match with the group at Halloween Havoc that will allow him to get his revenge once and for all.

articles.title: Top 5 College Football Coaches on the Hot Seat After Week 7 Ft. Steve Sarkisian
articles.summary: With Week 7 in the rearview mirror, some college football coaches are more secure than ever. Meanwhile, others are not.
articles.body:
With Week 7 in the rearview mirror, some college football coaches are more secure than ever. Meanwhile, others are not. Some coaches might not see January. For some, a year-long pattern of struggle is too much to explain away. For others, a sudden decline in a must-win year could be enough.

Here's a look at the top five college coaches most at risk of being cut loose in the coming weeks.

Steve Sarkisian Joins Top 5 Least Secure College Football Coaches

Steve Sarkisian seemed to be trending up earlier this season, but brutal back-to-back losses to unranked foes have turned everything on its head, with Texas tumbling from No. 1 to No. 19 in two weeks. Despite having the most hyped quarterback in college football, the Longhorns (4-2) appear to be imploding after consecutive 27-24 losses to the Florida Gators and Oklahoma Sooners, in which they had double-digit leads in the first half and crucial fourth-quarter turnovers.

At this point, if the free fall continues, the program could end up losing Arch Manning or moving on from Sarkisian. Someone has to go, and it could be that the only way to keep Manning is to let Sarkisian go.

Dan Lanning has lost only three games in a season once in his run with the Oregon Ducks. It was his first year with the program. With still half the season to go, Lanning has two losses. Sometimes, a veteran player's numbers in their final season will resemble their first year. If the same happens for Lanning, it could be his final run in Oregon.

Lanning has faced consistent criticism, as his Ducks (4-2) lost 17-15 to then-No. 21 UCLA and 39-31 at unranked Oklahoma State. The program also barely beat the unranked Nebraska Cornhuskers 17-14 in Week 7. With the Ducks, who were ranked No. 2 in the preseason poll, now outside the Top 25, it's a scary place for Lanning to be with a program accustomed to being a perennial contender.

Brent Venables is at risk of turning in more losing seasons than winning seasons in his five years with the Oklahoma Sooners. If that happens, it will be hard for him to explain away the consistent downturns. The Sooners have a history of excellence with Bob Stoops, Barry Switzer and Bud Wilkinson and will have no reason to settle if Venables can't get it done.

At 3-3 and 1-2 in SEC play , the program is closer to another losing season and has already been kicked out of the Top 25 AP Poll after starting the season at No. 10. If the Sooners don't get back into the rankings by the end of the season, the writing might be on the wall.

Remember when Diego Pavia and Clark Lea exploded in 2025? 2026 has been the opposite. Without Pavia, Lea's Commodores (3-4) are 0-4 in SEC play this year, and four of their next five foes are ranked. At this point, it was clear that Pavia was the key to the team's success. Once the players become more important to a college program than the coach, it is hard to rationalize keeping him.

Lea only has one season with double-digit wins and could finish with a losing record in four of his six seasons since taking over in 2021.

Deion Sanders stole headlines due to the unique situation of coaching Shedeur Sanders (and 2024 Heisman Trophy winner Travis Hunter). However, without his son at quarterback, the Buffaloes have struggled mightily. Sanders needed a big surge after three wins in 2025. Instead, it has been more of the same. Once struggle becomes predictable, it is time to look elsewhere.

Sanders' Buffaloes are 2-4 and have lost four straight games. It doesn't appear to be a question of if, but when he will be released. Coach Prime, who is 18-25 at CU, still has the job for now, and as long as he is still present on the sideline, he will not give up. However, things are as dire as they have ever been for the former Dallas Cowboys and Atlanta Falcons legend.

articles.title: “It’s Perplexing Why He’s Not the Quarterback”: Urban Meyer Questions Ryan Day’s Decision on Ohio State’s Five-Star QB
articles.summary: Ohio State endured a significant loss during its 19-15 win over Indiana on Saturday. Quarterback Julian Sayin suffered an injury to his throwing arm midway t...
articles.body:
Ohio State endured a significant loss during its 19-15 win over Indiana on Saturday. Quarterback Julian Sayin suffered an injury to his throwing arm midway through the fourth quater, necessitating a sling. He's expected to miss several weeks, with a return date not established.

To everyone's surprise, Luke Fahey, a 5-foot-11 true freshman who was a four-star prospect, took over at quarterback following the injury. Sophomore Tavien St. Clair, a highly touted former five-star prospect who is 6-4, stayed on the bench, in what has become a somewhat controversial decision by Ryan Day.

On the "Triple Option" podcast on Monday, former Ohio State coach Urban Meyer criticized the decision.

"It's perplexing why he's not the quarterback. You know, why he doesn't jog on the field when Sayin went down?" Meyer said .

Despite the late injury, Sayin was still the leading passer for the Buckeyes over the weekend. In the 19-15 win over the Hoosiers, Sayin threw for 235 yards, with two touchdown passes and two interceptions. Fahey only had two pass attempts during the game, both incompletions.

What did Ryan Day say about Julian Sayin's injury?

On Monday evening, Ryan Day spoke about the Julian Sayin injury on a local radio show in Columbus. His answer was, at best, unspecific about Sayin's situation.

Here's what the Buckeyes coach said about his quarterback:

"It'll be at least several weeks, but no update right now," Day said during the "Buckeye Roundtable" show on 97.1 The Fan in Columbus. "They're still going through some of their testing and some of their meetings."

Sayin was considered one of the favorites for the Heisman Trophy up until he was injured. He has 2,007 passing yards (third in the country), with 19 touchdown passes (third) and four interceptions. He ranked 10th among signal-callers in the FBS in QBR, with a rating of 84.5.

Last season, Julian Sayin was a Heisman Trophy finalist.

Just when fans were getting hopes up for a return of Myles Garrett, the Los Angeles Rams were hit with a wave of injuries unlike anything they've seen in a single week since 2022. Garrett is not going to return this week and Sean McVay can't give any updates on when he might return, while Terrance Ferguson isn't going to come back to practice yet either. Trent McDuffie's status is unclear.

The Rams announced once clear replacement for one of those injuries, which is Brandon McManus as the new kicker to replace Blake Grupe .

How else will the Rams look different when they face the Las Vegas Raiders?

Nobody is saying that Mumpfield will "replace" Adams in a production or value sense, and nobody's saying that McVay should not increase snaps or reps for Tutu Atwell and other options, including C.J. Daniels. But merely on the depth chart, player to player, Mumpfield is the next man up to start in place of Adams moving forward.

Adams gave Mumpfield a shoutout in the offseason as a receiver to watch out for, and now the second-year wideout gets to prove himself in that exact role.

A seventh-round pick in 2025, Mumpfield has 127 yards on eight catches. 48 of those yards came on a play where it didn't even feel like he was covered, he just juked someone out of position a little bit and the wheel route was on. Mumpfield has 178 snaps compared to 107 for Jordan Whittington.

Expect Atwell to be active, but what about Daniels? Or is Daniels active but not Atwell? Don't put any decision past McVay.

Davis should be stout against the run, but won't provide the same pass rushing presence as Turner. He has limited moves in his arsenal and below-average length.

The Rams went into the season as a "super group" on the defensive line. Now they're down to Byron Young as perhaps the only healthy player with a good track record who is having a good season.

Davis has played 146 snaps this season and he has 15 tackles. He had 43 tackles last season and he has 1.5 sacks in 2.5 years. The Rams must continue to seek other options on the defensive line.

Hamilton is another defensive lineman with a reputation for run defense, but not pass rushing ability. At least in this case, he's replacing another player who can't rush the passer. In fact, Ford might be the worst pass rusher at the nose tackle position in the entire league.

Hamilton has great power and leverage but he has limited pass rushing moves and is known to over-pursue when he gets the chance to play, which is rarely.

The Rams also have Larrell Murchison but he's only appeared in one game. That's sure to change.

On the practice squad, the Rams have Bill Norton and Jaxson Moi.

Coming into this season, Essenuge has something to prove. He will likely be relegated to vying for rotation minutes off the bench. Head coach Tiago Splitter has criticized Essenuge's physicality, which adds pressure on him to perform.

articles.title: Ohio State faces a major test without Julian Sayin
articles.summary: Who will be the Buckeyes' next signal caller in Sayin's absence?
articles.body:
Ohio State Buckeyes quarterback Julian Sayin has been ruled out indefinitely. Ryan Day announced the news Tuesday.

Sayin sustained the injury Saturday in the 19-15 win over No. 6 Indiana after a hit from Mario Landino. Landino came from around the edge and delivered a killing blow to Sayin's throwing shoulder.

True freshman Luke Fahey took over after Sayin's injury and went 0-for-2. Tavien St. Clair Jr. and Fahey will both get first-team reps in practice.

There's no doubt Sayin is the guy at quarterback, and head coach Ryan Day understands how important he is to the offense.

"This is all bigger than just one person," Day said post-game. "Certainly we don't want to see him get hurt, and we need him. At the same time, we'll come together and figure this out. We've got a good team. When Luke's in there, we just may need to do things just a little bit differently, but the bye week gives us a chance to regroup on that and put our heads together."

Sayin has 2,007 passing yards, 19 passing touchdowns, four interceptions, completes 68.2% of his passes this year, and was back in the Heisman Trophy conversation.

Before exiting the game against Indiana, Sayin had two touchdown passes and boosted the Buckeyes' lead to 12.

Sayin has no return date, but the Buckeyes are preparing for the rest of the season and playoffs without him, per ESPN's Pete Thamel.

Ohio State still has five games remaining on the schedule and faces 16th-ranked USC, a new and improved 24th-ranked Northwestern, and The Game against Michigan.

articles.title: Bears' Caleb Williams could miss out on MVP for one reason
articles.summary: Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams may already be out of the MVP running. Maybe.
articles.body:
Caleb Williams of the Chicago Bears is having the kind of run that could earn him the MVP award, but that doesn't mean it's going to happen. There's a lot of football left to play, and one major factor could keep him out of the race.

In a feature released on Tuesday, Ben Solak of ESPN notes that Williams could certainly be up for the honor, but missing time is a huge detriment to his chances of winning it. In the piece, he predicts that Williams "will end up an MVP candidate who missed too much time."

Caleb Williams' MVP hopes could survive his missed games, but the Bears quarterback still has a major hurdle to overcome

In the piece, Solak makes the case that if Williams keeps performing well while putting up the big numbers he's bringing to the table, the NFL won't be able to ignore him, even with the missed time.

He says that if Williams "continues to play high-percentage ball while adding the playmaking ability afforded by his legs and authoring a couple of heroic late-game throws in high-leverage spots, then he's going to look like an MVP by December. And we will all be forced to reconcile with the missed games and whatever other narratives have developed about the other candidates since."

But the MVP race is always a tough one, so missing three games could hurt. One positive is that Williams missed those games early in the season, so Solak notes that voters may almost forget he was out by the time voting rolls around. If the Bears go deep in the playoffs, that would obviously help his case, too.

articles.title: Caleb Lomu Shatters Rookie Tackle Grades After Injury Surge
articles.summary: Rookie Caleb Lomu posted the league's best pass-blocking grades after injuries forced him into the lineup. Here is the surprising data from Sunday's win.
articles.body:
The biggest surprise in the Patriots' 26-19 win over the Jets isn't the final score. It is the performance of a rookie who wasn't supposed to play this much. Caleb Lomu, the 28th overall pick, now holds the top pass-blocking grade among all rookie tackles in the NFL. This comes after injuries to starters Will Campbell and Morgan Moses forced the 21-year-old into the spotlight during Sunday's game.

Lomu was drafted to sit on the bench behind veteran Morgan Moses and Will Campbell. The team traded up four spots to get the 6-foot-6, 313-pound tackle from Utah. He was expected to be a backup depth piece for heavy sets. Instead, he became the most effective pass protector on the offensive line. Per Sports Illustrated , Lomu earned an 80.2 pass-blocking grade through six weeks. That number leads the entire rookie class. His pass-blocking efficiency sits at a 98.0, which is also the highest mark for any rookie tackle.

Campbell suffered a knee injury and Moses dealt with a foot issue in the past two games. These setbacks gave Lomu extended playing time on the right side. He played out of position since he lined up at left tackle in college. Despite the switch, he dominated his new role. Head coach Mike Vrabel addressed the situation after Sunday's game. "I hate when guys get injured, but I also understand that on the other side of that, there's an opportunity," Vrabel said. He added, "You never know what's going to happen in this league, and we talk about it all the time, preparing for the journey."

Lomu knew this day could come before the season even started. Marcus Bryant was slated to be the sixth offensive lineman, but Bryant has been sidelined for most of the year. This opened the door for Lomu to take more snaps. Lomu explained his mindset on filling in for injured starters. "It does happen, unfortunately, in this league. Everyone's got to prepare like a starter for those types of things that happen," Lomu said. The team traded up to get him for a reason, and now that reason is showing up in the stats.

The offensive line looked ragged, yet the team secured the victory. Pats Pulpit noted the strange lineup that defeated the Jets. Despite starting a rookie at right tackle, a third-string guard on one side, and a fourth-string guard on the other, the Patriots ran the ball effectively. The free-agent fullback was even on injured reserve. Steve Balestrieri issued a Week 6 report card with a simple message: "Never apologize for a win." The receivers got demerits for their struggles, but the line held up enough to get the job done.

DeMario Douglas stepped up at receiver while Romeo Doubs sits on injured reserve. Despite committing a fumble against the Jets, Douglas caught three touchdowns over the last two games. He acknowledged the team needs to fix its errors. "I feel like we've just got to learn. We can learn from our mistakes," he said postgame.

Lomu's rise proves the depth chart is deeper than it looked on paper. He is now the right tackle of New England's future, according to the data. The Patriots face the Chicago Bears on Thursday night. Lomu must maintain these grades while protecting Drake Maye.

WASHINGTON (AP) — Top draft pick AJ Dybantsa will miss the season opener for the Washington Wizards on Wednesday night with a sprained ankle.

Coach Brian Keefe said Tuesday that Dybantsa would not play against the Milwaukee Bucks. The Wizards took him No. 1 out of BYU in this year's draft.

Dybantsa is one of the reasons hopes are higher in Washington than in the recent past. The Wizards also added veterans Trae Young and Anthony Davis last season, but Davis didn't play at all in a Washington uniform. He's back now .

Dybantsa's debut will have to wait. The Wizards are also home Friday night against Toronto.

"He's going to be day to day," Keefe said.

articles.title: Jeremy Fears Jr. returns to UConn vs MSU exhibition after injury scare
articles.summary: All-American point guard Jeremy Fears Jr. landed hard on a driving layup, grabbing at his lower left leg and foot during Michigan State's exhibition.
articles.body:
EAST LANSING - All-American point guard Jeremy Fears Jr. landed hard on a driving layup, grabbing at his lower left leg and foot during Michigan State basketball's exhibition game with Connecticut on Tuesday, Oct. 20.

The preseason national and Big Ten player of the year landed on the Huskies' Colben Landrew with 17:53 left in the second half. Fears grabbed at his left ankle and lower leg while laying on the court. He got back up and hobbled to the bench, checking himself out of the game and immediately going to the training staff.

His stay was brief. Fears received treatment and checked back into the game with 15:44 to play, with coach Tom Izzo telling him to take it easy.

That scare came after the 6-foot-2 point guard had an electric tomahawk dunk in the first half over Landrew.

articles.title: Kevin Byard looking forward to return to Chicago to face Bears, Caleb Williams

articles.body:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. (AP) — New England Patriots safety Kevin Byard doesn't have any hard feelings about the two seasons he spent with the Chicago Bears .

But this week he is trying to think of any tips to help his new team walk out of Thursday's night matchup in Chicago with a victory against his former team.

"I'm giving the coaches and the players as much as I can, you know what I mean?" Byard said with a smile on Tuesday. "Obviously, I am not there anymore, and I don't have all my notes and stuff like that. But as far as personnel, anything I can kind of remember."

Byard experienced plenty during his two seasons with the Bears.

He arrived in 2024 after his lone season in Philadelphia, signed a two-year deal and was selected as a captain on his new team. He then proceeded to be part of a rebuilding year that included coach Matt Eberflus being fired after 12 games in what ended up being a 10-game losing streak.

The Bears quickly turned things around last season under new coach Ben Johnson, and Byard thrived in the new environment, leading the NFL in interceptions while being selected as an All-Pro for the third time in his career.

It's why the main feeling he's taking with him when he returns to Soldier Field this week is one of respect.

"Definitely excited to go back to Chicago and play up there," Byard said. "I loved playing in that stadium in front of those fans. It's going to be an electric environment."

Part of Byard's experience over the past two seasons was getting to know Bears quarterback Caleb Williams, who was his fellow captain both years.

Williams said he learned a lot from Byard during their time together.

"Obviously, being able to go versus him, practice for two years. I mean, he's a super savvy vet," Williams said. "I know he's getting up there in age (laughs), but he's still fast, and he does — I've seen him work. He studies film. He still moves extremely well. He knows the route concepts really well."

It's given the Patriots an extra lift to a secondary that already includes star Christian Gonzalez.

Johnson isn't surprised that Byard has fit in so well in New England's locker room.

"I love Kevin Byard and what he brings to the table. You can tell he really fits their defense well in terms of the communication and what they're asking him to do," Johnson said.

Though Byard has yet to have an INT through the Patriots first six games, Williams said he'll be keeping an eye on him this week.

"It's gonna be a great challenge for us, a great challenge for me and the wide receivers to be able to go out there and execute and complete passes and keep being the offense and identity that we wanna be," Williams said.

"I love his mentality, I'm a huge fan of him, honestly," Byard said. "I just think the care, his willingness to go out there and fight every day with his team. So I'm excited to play against him and hopefully our defense can have a better day."

articles.title: Report: Michigan Football QB Tommy Carr to make first career start vs Indiana
articles.summary: Per reports, Michigan Football QB Tommy Carr will make his first career start against Indiana on Saturday:
articles.body:
As first reported by 247Sports on Tuesday night, Michigan true freshman quarterback Tommy Carr is set to make the first start of his career against the No. 6 Indiana Hoosiers on Saturday afternoon.

Carr was thrust into the spotlight after being called on to replace starting quarterback Bryce Underwood against Penn State, and the freshman signal-caller fueled Michigan to a 21-18 comeback win.

The Wolverines were in complete disarray on offense — trailing 3-0 at halftime with Underwood at the helm. But that all changed when Carr entered the game and instantly provided a much-needed spark for Michigan .

Carr proceeded to lead three scoring drives in the second half, highlighted by a 12-yard, game-clinching touchdown run late in the game. He completed 5-for-7 passes and compiled 83 total yards and one touchdown.

It became clear Michigan needed a change after Underwood threw two interceptions in a scoreless first half against Penn State, and Carr's impact was palpable. Now, the freshman quarterback gets his chance to start.

Prior to his appearance against Penn State, Carr only played in one other game this season. In a blowout win over UTEP, Carr completed 2-for-2 passing attempts for 23 yards and one touchdown. He also had two carries for 18 rushing yards.

The 6-foot-4, 195-pound quarterback is the grandson of legendary former Michigan head coach Lloyd Carr, who led the program to the 1997 national championship. Nearly three decades later, his grandson will start for the very first time against the reigning national champions.
